The six classical calendar variation models

Source: R/classic.R
calvar_classic_all.Rd

Fits the six combinations of trend (deterministic or stochastic) and seasonality (dummy, Fourier or stochastic) of [calvar_classic()], named `m1` to `m6` as in its table, for one or several calendar designs.

Usage

calvar_classic_all(
  y,
  dates,
  K = frequency(y)/2 - 1,
  lambda = NULL,
  design = "dummy",
  window = list(before = "auto", holiday = c(0, 3)),
  window_grid = c(7, 14, 21, 28),
  ...
)

Arguments

y

Monthly or quarterly `ts`.

dates

`Date` vector of holiday occurrences.

K

Number of Fourier pairs for `season = "fourier"` (default 5 for monthly data).

lambda

Box-Cox parameter; `NULL` (default) keeps the original scale, so the holiday effect is additive.

design

One or more of `"dummy"`, `"leadlag"` and `"window"`. With several designs the models are named `m1_dummy`, `m1_leadlag`, ...

window

For `design = "window"`: a named list of windows `c(a, b)` in days relative to the holiday, one regressor (and one effect) per window. The default, `list(before = "auto", holiday = c(0, 3))`, chooses the length of the window before the holiday by AICc.

window_grid

Candidate lengths www (days) for a window given as `"auto"`, which then covers the www days before the holiday.

...

Passed to [forecast::auto.arima()].

Value

An object of class `"calvar_classic_set"`: a list with the fitted models (`models`), their specification (`spec`) and, for an automatic window, the AICc of every structure and candidate (`window_aicc`).

Details

With `design = "window"` and a window given as `"auto"`, every structure ranks the candidate windows by AICc, and the window chosen by most structures (the shorter one in a tie) is used for all six, so that their calendar regressors are the same.

Examples

# \donttest{
set <- calvar_classic_all(sapi, holiday_dates("idul_adha"))
set
#> 6 classical calendar variation models; holiday dummy
#>  model trend  season  ARIMA              AICc   holiday     
#>  m1    det.   dummy   (3,0,1)            1851.4 29.78 (1.72)
#>  m2    det.   Fourier (3,0,1)            1849.3 29.77 (1.72)
#>  m3    stoch. dummy   (2,1,2)            1843.1 29.78 (1.72)
#>  m4    stoch. Fourier (2,1,2)            1841.0 29.77 (1.73)
#>  m5    det.   stoch.  (1,0,2)(2,0,0)[12] 1718.2 17.61 (1.91)
#>  m6    stoch. stoch.  (1,1,1)(1,0,2)[12] 1708.9 18.92 (2.01)
#> Trend: det. = deterministic, stoch. = stochastic; seasonality: stoch. = seasonal ARIMA.
#> Holiday effects: estimate (s.e.); with the window design they are effects of a full window.
#> Note: AICc is comparable only between models with the same order of differencing.
fc <- forecast(set, h = 12)
names(fc)
#> [1] "m1" "m2" "m3" "m4" "m5" "m6"
# the 18 models of the three calendar designs
all18 <- calvar_classic_all(sapi, holiday_dates("idul_adha"),
                            design = c("dummy", "leadlag", "window"))
# }
